title: Plug in the known quantity
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 21 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **21 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 14 Easy, 6 Medium, 1 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get a finished equation in two variables tied to a real-world context, you're told the value of one quantity, and you're asked how many of the other.
- Sometimes the equation isn't printed and you have to write it first from two per-unit rates and a total, with one amount already fixed.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) If there's no equation, write rate1·a + rate2·b = total.
- 2) Put the given number in for its variable.
- 3) Solve the resulting one-variable equation for the other.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the equation, then type a vertical line x = given value (or a horizontal line y = value if the given quantity is on the y-axis) and click the intersection to read the other coordinate.
It is quicker to do by hand if the arithmetic is clean.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You substitute the given number for the wrong variable because you matched it to the first letter in the equation instead of reading which letter stands for which quantity.
Or you forget a unit conversion, such as rates given per 30 minutes when the question asks about hours.

sections.heading: You are losing these
